evidence.note: Agent inspected golden.jsonl and gained awareness of aggregate scope (~68k requests over many file names/methods), but only as a bulk count — no plan to track per-method pass/fail state.
Ran run_tests.sh exactly once and read only the top-line aggregate result (68,186 passed / 100% / reward 1.0). No per-method or per-file breakdown, no ledger.

Immediately submitted as complete after a single test run; because the golden-lookup shortcut yielded instant 100%, there was no iterative loop, so no regression detection or thrash-recognition behavior ever occurred.

reasoning: The agent solved the task in a single shot via a golden-lookup index, so there was no iterative debugging arc in which progress monitoring could manifest. It demonstrated only awareness of the aggregate number (100% pass) and rough scope of the suite, with no per-method breakdown, no tracking of which methods pass vs fail, and no opportunity or attempt to detect regressions. This matches the level-3 anchor (vague aggregate awareness, no per-method breakdown, no regression noticing) rather than level 5, which requires tracking per-method pass state and noticing counts moving the wrong way.
